name: Jarvis
blurb: An instrument that displays the machine's measured state.

tone.reason: Consonant clarity. Jarvis reports state and asks questions, and at ~120 Hz his fundamental sits an octave under the other characters, so the presence band is where his words are told apart rather than merely heard.
Boxiness. A male fundamental near 120 Hz puts strong second and third harmonics right here; they crowd the vowels rather than adding weight, and cutting reads as clarity, not thinness.

provenance.note: VOICE: two providers, two different jobs. `fish` is the GENERATION id -- it rendered the eight register references in pocket-voice/refs/jarvis/ via make_registers.py, and is not used at runtime. `pocket-voice: jarvis` IS the runtime voice: nine local clones (jarvis plus jarvis-<tag> for all eight registers), which cost nothing per call and keep the audio on the box. A tag maps to a voice STATE rather than a parameter because Pocket TTS's contract has no emotion, style, speed or pitch field -- a tone written into the text would simply be read aloud. The eight picks were made on duration closest to 7.0s, a measurable proxy, and are PROVISIONAL: register fit is an ear judgement, and re-choosing in me-lora's bench overwrites the same names. Jarvis was registered inline in characters.ts while Familiar came from a bundle; this manifest makes both bodies the same kind of thing. He names his OWN canvas source: the shader source supplies the Familiar's uniform set, and Jarvis needs a different one entirely (budgets, work, speech, readout), so drawing him through it would have been refused at registration -- correctly. uGene is listed because the shader needs it, though JarvisRenderer uploads it once at mount rather than per frame. scripts/check_jarvis_shader.sh pins the vendored frag against its canon copy.
